nodes.content: Design runtime verification for multicore embedded controllers that preserves deadline guarantees and sound verdicts despite asynchronous, lossy telemetry.
requirements: Verdicts are sound under telemetry loss and complete for bounded-response violations when telemetry is lossless.
Monitoring adds ≤5% worst-case execution time per control job while preserving all specified deadlines.

nodes.content: Deploy 5%-budgeted per-core probes, synchronized timestamps, sequence-checked heartbeat watermarks, three-valued bounded-response monitors, and deadline response-time analysis.
How can bounded-response monitoring distinguish missing telemetry from absent responses without exceeding per-job overhead or invalidating deadline guarantees?
Skew-aware, gap-checked watermarks prevent false alarms under loss and catch lossless response violations; budgeted probes preserve deadlines at ≤5% WCET.
Run four-core fault-injection at 0–20% telemetry loss and 50-µs skew; measure verdict soundness, lossless violation recall, WCET, and deadline slack.
Four-core trials: zero false verdicts (0–20% loss), 100% lossless violation recall, 4.2% peak WCET overhead, 120-µs minimum deadline slack.
Adopt gap-checked watermark monitoring for the tested four-core configuration: zero false verdicts, full lossless violation recall, and preserved deadline slack.
Following adoption, implement gap-to-unknown and skew-bounded, gap-free timeout rules; statically certify ≤5% probe WCET and all job deadlines.
Implement RV-Core v1.0 sequence-gap detection and 50-µs-skew watermark gating; model-check that timeout alarms require complete response windows.
RV-Core v1.0 contains gap-aware monitor code, 50-µs-skew watermark gating, and a model-check report on complete-window timeout guards.
Statically bound RV-Core v1.0 probe WCET and multicore response times under worst-case telemetry bursts; check ≤5% overhead and deadlines.
Static RV-Core v1.0 analysis bounds probe WCET overhead at 4.8% and worst-case deadline slack at 80 µs under burst telemetry.
Window-local sequence-gap tracking should increase conclusive verdict coverage versus global suppression at 20% loss without changing soundness or probe WCET.
Run four-core 20%-loss injections with window-local versus global-gap suppression; measure conclusive-verdict coverage, false alarms, probe WCET, and deadline slack.
At 20% loss, window-local and global suppression each yielded 74% conclusive coverage; zero false alarms, 4.2% WCET overhead.
Formalize 50-µs skew and gap contracts; prove soundness and lossless violation completeness; certify ≤5% WCET overhead and deadlines across modes.
Model-check RV-Core v1.0 bounded-response verdicts in TLA+ under 50-µs skew, asynchronous delivery, and arbitrary drops for soundness and lossless completeness.
RV-Core TLA+ v1.0 package contains an asynchronous-loss model, 50-µs skew assumptions, and soundness and lossless-violation completeness checks.
Use ≤5%-WCET shared-memory probes, overflow-marked event rings, and a reserved-time monitor that judges only complete bounded-response windows.
What ring capacity and monitor reservation ensure overflow is reported and four-core control deadlines survive worst-case event bursts?
256-slot rings and a 150-µs/ms monitor reservation should flag overflows and preserve deadlines at 64 events/ms/core with ≤5% probe WCET.
Using RV-Core TLA+ verdicts, compare watermark and 256-slot ring monitors with 150-µs/ms reservation at 64 events/ms/core: overflow, soundness, WCET, deadlines.
At 64 events/ms/core, ring reservation caused 30-µs deadline misses; watermark monitoring retained 80-µs slack at 4.8% probe overhead.
Reject the 150-µs/ms ring reservation and retain RV-Core watermark monitoring: only the ring configuration missed deadlines under burst load.
Replacing reservation with slack-stealing 256-slot ring drains should flag overflow, preserve deadlines, and maintain ≤5% overhead at 64 events/ms/core.
Using RV-Core TLA+ verdicts, stress 256-slot slack-stealing rings at 64 events/ms/core and forced overflow; check flags, soundness, WCET, deadlines.
At 64 events/ms/core, all forced overflows were flagged; zero false verdicts, 4.9% peak probe WCET, 25-µs minimum deadline slack.
Implement 256-slot slack-stealing rings; certify overflow flags, ≤5% probe WCET, and deadlines at 64 events/ms/core.
Instrument four-core control jobs with 256-slot rings and slack-only drains; test overflow signaling at 64 events/ms/core.
RingProbe v1.0 adds four-core 256-slot event rings, overflow markers, and slack-only draining, plus 64-events/ms/core stress-test logs.
Integrate RingProbe v1.0 with RV-Core v1.0; certify ≤5% probe WCET, deadlines, overflow-to-unknown verdicts, and lossless violation recall.
Integrated tests: 4.9% probe WCET overhead, 25-µs deadline slack, 100% lossless violation recall; overflow windows unknown, zero false verdicts.
Retain statically certified RV-Core baseline; gate overflow-tested RingProbe deployment on deadline proof because integration leaves only 25-µs measured slack.
Deploy per-core automata over timestamped shared-memory logs; sequence verdicts, mark gaps unknown, and certify ≤5% WCET and deadlines.
Specify per-core automata and log contracts; prove gap-aware bounded-response verdicts sound and lossless-complete; certify ≤5% WCET and deadlines.
Extend RV-Core TLA+ v1.0 with per-core log automata; check gap-aware verdict soundness and lossless violation completeness under 50-µs skew.
LogAutomata TLA+ v1.1 adds per-core timestamped-log transitions, sequence-gap unknown states, and 50-µs-skew verdict-check specifications.
What watermark-progress assumption lets LogAutomata v1.1 close cross-core response windows despite unbounded log delay and 50-µs clock skew?
Eventually delivered, gap-free per-core watermarks beyond each deadline plus 50 µs ensure sound closure and lossless-violation completeness.
Model-check LogAutomata v1.1 cross-core closures under 50-µs skew and arbitrary delays/drops; verify soundness and lossless completeness with eventual gap-free watermarks.
LogAutomata v1.1 checks found zero false closures with 50-µs skew and drops; lossless violations flagged under eventual gap-free watermarks.
Require eventual gap-free watermarks for lossless-completeness claims; otherwise leave unresolved windows unknown rather than report violations.
Benchmark watermark-gated LogAutomata against RingProbe at 64 events/ms/core, 0–20% loss; measure false verdicts, lossless recall, WCET, deadline slack.
At 64 events/ms/core, LogAutomata: zero false verdicts, 100% lossless recall, 4.6% WCET overhead, 55-µs slack; RingProbe: 4.9%, 25 µs.
What bound on shared-memory cache-coherence stalls preserves LogAutomata’s 55-µs measured slack during simultaneous four-core bursts?
Capping coherence stalls at 0.3% job WCET and 10 µs response time should preserve ≤5% overhead and ≥45-µs slack.
With gap-free watermarks, stress LogAutomata v1.1 on four cores; check 0.3%-WCET/10-µs coherence bounds, ≤5% overhead, ≥45-µs slack.
Four-core bursts caused 5.4% probe WCET overhead and 12-µs deadline misses despite 0.2%-WCET coherence stalls and 8-µs delays.
Retain statically certified RV-Core baseline (4.8% overhead); defer RingProbe pending deadline proof and LogAutomata after burst deadline misses.
Release RV-Core after per-mode soundness, lossless-completeness, ≤5% WCET and deadline checks; gate RingProbe, defer LogAutomata.
Verify RingProbe v1.0 across control modes against RV-Core: overflow-to-unknown verdicts, lossless violation recall, ≤5% probe WCET, and deadline proofs.
RingProbe v1.1 revises v1.0 with per-mode deployment gates and bundles overflow-to-unknown, lossless-recall, WCET, and deadline verification reports.
Compare RV-Core v1.0 and gated RingProbe v1.1 across control modes; audit verdict proofs, ≤5% WCET, and deadline certificates.
Gated RingProbe modes certified 4.9% probe WCET overhead, ≥18-µs deadline slack, zero false verdicts, and 100% lossless violation recall.
Enable RingProbe in certified modes, retain RV-Core elsewhere, and defer LogAutomata despite 4.6% nominal overhead after burst deadline misses.
